register.name: Treasury securities outstanding
register.detail: US Treasury · Monthly Treasury Statement, close of October 2026 · up $352.7bn in October · debt held by the public $32.74tn
register.note: Budget-wide; $40.17 trillion at the close of fiscal year 2026, on 30 September 2026
register.text: The stock of securities issued by the US Treasury at the close of October 2026, $352.7 billion more than a month earlier; $32.74 trillion of it is debt held by the public. It funds the federal budget as a whole and is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Section 32 food purchase for food banks (October 2026)
register.detail: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service · announced 29 October 2026 · Section 32 authority · up to $472.5M across 15 products
register.text: American-grown food bought from farmers and delivered to food banks and nutrition programs: dairy, pulses, nuts, fruit, rice, pork, chicken and fish.

register.name: USDA Rural Development loans and grants, fiscal year 2026
register.detail: USDA Rural Development · announced 7 October 2026 · fiscal year to 30 September 2026 · in West Virginia, $184.2M for housing and $34.2M for water and wastewater systems
register.note: Nearly $25 billion nationwide; more than $265.9 million of it in West Virginia
register.text: Investment by USDA Rural Development in rural communities across the nation in fiscal year 2026. In West Virginia alone its loans and grants financed homeownership and affordable rental housing, water and wastewater systems, hospitals and other community facilities, small businesses and internet access, which carry the shelter, water, health and livelihood standards.

register.name: CDFI Fund awards: CDFI, NACA, Bank Enterprise Award and Small Dollar Loan Programs
register.detail: US Treasury, CDFI Fund · announced 15 September 2026 · FY 2025 CDFI Program and Native American CDFI Assistance Program awards · FY 2026 Bank Enterprise Award and Small Dollar Loan Program awards · awardees notified by 30 September 2026
register.note: The release does not state the amounts awarded
register.text: Treasury awards to community development financial institutions, Native American CDFIs and banks serving underserved communities, made from appropriations that would have expired on 30 September 2026. CDFI Program financial assistance can fund financial products, loan loss reserves and capital reserves, and the awards are meant to help small businesses expand and create jobs, which carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: Section 32 food purchase for schools and food banks (August 2026)
register.detail: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service · announced 24 August 2026 · Section 32 of the Agriculture Act of 1935 · up to $156M across eight products
register.text: American-grown food bought from producers for schools and food banks through the National School Lunch Program and The Emergency Food Assistance Program: walnuts, pork, mandarins, raisins, grape juice, shrimp, prunes and canned peaches. It carries the food standard for children and families who rely on school meals and food banks.

register.name: Healthy Food Financing Partnerships, 2026 round
register.detail: Reinvestment Fund for USDA · opened 29 June 2026 · grants of $200,000 to $3 million
register.text: Grants to the public-private partnerships that finance grocers and food enterprises in their own state or region.

register.name: Healthy Food Financing Initiative, FARE Fund
register.detail: Reinvestment Fund for USDA Rural Development · 2024-25 rounds, completed 16 April 2026
register.note: $9 million in grants, $6 million in loans, $1.5 million in technical assistance
register.text: Grants and loans to 62 food retail and supply chain projects in 39 states, 30 of them rural.

register.name: Section 32 food purchase for food banks (February 2026)
register.detail: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service · announced 19 February 2026 · Section 32 of the Agriculture Act of 1935 · up to $263M across 12 products
register.text: Dairy products, dried beans, chickpeas, lentils, split peas, pears and nuts bought from American producers for food banks and nutrition assistance programs, including The Emergency Food Assistance Program. It carries the food standard through the charitable food network.

register.name: Pennsylvania Fresh Food Financing Initiative
register.detail: Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and Reinvestment Fund · 2004 to 2010
register.note: State seed money, leveraged with $145 million in additional investment
register.text: Loans and grants for 88 fresh food retail projects in underserved urban and rural communities; the model for the national Healthy Food Financing Initiative.

register.name: Ursa Re 2026-1 catastrophe bond
register.detail: Ursa Re Ltd. for the California Earthquake Authority · priced in November 2026 · about four years · indemnity trigger, annual aggregate · Class D $500M at a 3.5% spread · Class H $400M at an 8% spread
register.note: Upsized from a $600 million target; the second-largest cat bond the Authority has sponsored directly
register.text: Fully collateralized California earthquake reinsurance from capital market investors for the California Earthquake Authority, the state’s earthquake insurer. It helps the insurer pay claims after a major earthquake, which bears on the shelter standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 17.1% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Oil and Gas
items.label: Of GDP from oil and gas rents, 2021
items.text: Oil and gas already earn; the task is to turn the rent into assets that outlast it.

enterprises.heading: Already working in the United States.

items.name: DC Central Kitchen
items.text: A Washington, DC non-profit that runs a culinary job training programme with 161 graduates a year and earns its own revenue through three social enterprise cafés and its school food service, which serves 12,000 meals a day at 30 schools, within a regular output of 17,000 meals a day in 2025.

items.name: Champlain Housing Trust
items.text: A community land trust in northwest Vermont with 2,929 affordable apartments and 706 shared equity homes, which signed 337 new leases in fiscal year 2025, 94 of them with formerly homeless households, and earned 32.2% of its income from rent.

items.name: GRID Alternatives
items.text: A non-profit that designs, installs and maintains solar and clean energy systems for economic and environmental justice communities across the country, and administers California’s Disadvantaged Communities Single-Family Solar Homes programme, which installed a record 3,076 kW in 2025.

items.name: Civica Rx
items.text: A non-profit generic drug company created by US health systems and philanthropies to prevent and mitigate drug shortages, which supplies more than 50 drugs to 60 health systems with 1,400 hospitals and runs its own sterile injectable plant in Petersburg, Virginia.
items.source: US Senate Special Committee on Aging, 2025

items.name: Homeboy Industries
items.text: A Los Angeles organisation for formerly gang-involved and previously incarcerated people that runs an 18-month programme for over 450 people a year and offers more than 300 jobs and training places in its 15 social enterprises, among them Homeboy Bakery and Homegirl Café.
